Fuck yield and diseases and all that, in this thread we're just talking about flavor. Also yes, I post a lot of threads because this is the best subverse ever and I've been obsessed with gardening edible plants lately. Flowers and whatever are cool but I love edible plants.

Anyway... those of you who have grown white, green, orange, yellow, blue/purple/black, or striped (or anything I forgot), please tell us what the flavor and texture qualities were like.

The rest of this post is opinion/thinking out loud beyond this point if you want to ignore it.

I've read green tomatoes are kind of... just? not good? Not sure how else to put it. A lot of the reviews on rareseeds say they still taste unripe even when they're fully ripe, and more objective descriptions call them tart/acidic and not very sweet. I personally think that kind of sounds like something that's not worth my time growing. I grew a hybrid that was Cherokee x Carbon (surprisingly enough called Cherokee Carbon) last year and holy shit they were good. They must have had a ton of glutamate in them, they were super savory, and perfectly balanced between meaty and juicy. Putting a little salt on those made it feel like my mouth was having an orgasm pretty much. They did take forever to grow but they were also not in a good area for light so that was probably my fault.

I'm seeing yellow/orange and especially white described as super sweet and fruity. In fact one variety I'm growing this year is a white grape/cherry tomato and it's claimed to be super sweet. I'm not sure I really want my culinary vegetables to taste like fruit, other than a handful of small grape tomatoes. I just don't think a beefsteak/slicer that tastes like mangoes or melon or whatever sounds good on a sandwich or anything raw or cooked or preserved. Raw by itself sounds maybe alright, but nothing on it...

Dunno. Lots of thinking out loud here. Let me know what you think.
Does/has anyone grown non-standard color tomatoes? What did you think of the flavor?
I'll let you know. Trying black/blue tomatoes this year. Never had a bad yellow tomato though.

What is the flavor of the yellow ones like? Is it more similar to red tomatoes than most people would let on? Reviews and bloggers are all like "omg it's so fruity and sweet", I mean, I feel like it can't be THAT big of a difference, but at the same time I don't want my tomatoes to taste like their parents had sex with a mango.

It stills tastes like a tomato. I never had a tomato that was overwhelming sweet, I feel like bloggers are just fluffers.

That being said ground cherries sort of taste like a tomato/sour mango hybrid.
Sounds like I have some experimenting to do then, as long as it's not going to taste like someone tried to cross a tomato with tropical fruit, that just sounds unappealing lol
Yeah, only one way to find out. I've tasted so many cool things that were the result of me growing them. Never even seen some things in the store.

I had carbon (deep purple) tomatoes and bright (neon road cone level) orange cherry tomatoes in my last garden.

I am not much of a tomato person. I like them cooked into sauces, but not really raw. That being said, the cherry tomatoes were out of this world incredibly delicious. I think they were a bit more acidic than a typical tomato, and sweet as heck. I miss them and crave them bigly.

The carbon ones were good - I liked them better than the other ones we had (they were pink/red striped with some yellow. Really pretty). Super hearty, meaty tomato. Unfortunately, we didn't get to eat many of the carbon blacks or the pink ones because goddamn worms moved in and ate the shit out of them. Live and learn. We'll be better prepared for culling pests next year.

Pretty sure the cherry tomatoes are "Sweet 100". Highly recommend!
Yellow and purple ones from my mom's garden are great. Not sure what kind they are. Reminds me of cherry tomatoes, but they are bigger.
